issues_encountered: test_basic_miss_then_hit and test_fence_i_invalidation both asserting ic_stall_o=0 after 1 rising edge — too soon for 2-cycle hit FSM

Initial fix attempt added 2 RisingEdge waits total (per knowledge.md suggestion) but still failed: knowledge.md suggestion was itself incorrect — it failed to account for the edge where _fetch() returns (CS_TAG_CHECK) and the FSM still needs one more clock to reach CS_IDLE before the new lookup can begin
fixes_applied: test_basic_miss_then_hit line 163-169: replaced 1 RisingEdge with 3 RisingEdge waits with cycle-by-cycle comments explaining FSM state at each edge
test_fence_i_invalidation line 296-305: same 1→3 RisingEdge fix with matching comments
Updated knowledge.md: corrected the wrong fix suggestion (was: 2 edges, actual: 3) and documented the _fetch() return-point subtlety
notes: Key subtlety: _fetch() returns at the CS_TAG_CHECK rising edge where stall first deasserts, NOT after it returns to CS_IDLE. The re-assertion of ic_valid_i takes one full clock cycle for CS_TAG_CHECK→CS_IDLE transition before the new lookup CS_IDLE→CS_SRAM_LATCH→CS_TAG_CHECK adds 2 more edges. phase3_all result: icache 7/7 PASS, dcache 8/8 PASS, cache_integration 5/5 PASS.
